articleBody:
Replacing your bathroom floor involves more than picking out a surface finish. A successful remodel requires checking the plumbing, prepping the substrate, and coordinating trim. Use this checklist to make sure your project stays on track from start to finish.

- [ ] Subfloor moisture test — Check for hidden dampness or rot around toilets and tubs before selecting materials.
- [ ] Finished floor height measurement — Verify that new flooring and underlayment will align cleanly with adjoining bedroom or hallway flooring.
- [ ] Slip resistance rating check — Pick a wet-area rated surface texture to prevent slip-and-fall hazards when stepping out of showers.
- [ ] Toilet shutoff valve inspection — Confirm the supply valve turns off completely so plumbing can be disconnected without house-wide shutoffs.
- [ ] Replacement wax ring or gasket ready — Secure a new seal to reinstall the toilet properly over the updated floor height.
- [ ] Vanity footprint decision — Decide whether the new floor goes wall-to-wall underneath the vanity or cuts around existing cabinetry.
- [ ] Baseboard and trim plan — Determine if current baseboards will be lifted and reset or replaced with moisture-resistant trim.
- [ ] Written contractor scope of work — Ensure subfloor leveling and trash disposal are documented in writing before demolition begins.

How to use this checklist:
Review these concrete items with your contractor during your initial consultation. Addressing these points early avoids surprise change orders and keeps your renovation running smoothly.
